entries.name: a
entries.summary: The <a> HTML element (or anchor element), with its href attribute, creates a hyperlink to web pages, files, email addresses, locations in the same page, or anything else a URL can address.

entries.name: abbr
entries.summary: The <abbr> HTML element represents an abbreviation or acronym.

entries.name: accept (attribute)
entries.summary: The accept attribute takes as its value a comma-separated list of one or more file types, or unique file type specifiers, describing which file types to allow.

entries.name: accesskey (attribute)
entries.summary: The accesskey global attribute provides a hint for generating a keyboard shortcut for the current element.

entries.name: address
entries.summary: The <address> HTML element indicates that the enclosed HTML provides contact information for a person or people, or for an organization.

entries.name: anchor (attribute)
entries.summary: Non-standard: This feature is not standardized. We do not recommend using non-standard features in production, as they have limited browser support, and may change or be removed.

entries.name: area
entries.summary: The <area> HTML element defines an area inside an image map that has predefined clickable areas. An image map allows geometric areas on an image to be associated with hypertext links.

entries.name: article
entries.summary: The <article> HTML element represents a self-contained composition in a document, page, application, or site, which is intended to be independently distributable or reusable (e.g., in syndication).

entries.name: aside
entries.summary: The <aside> HTML element represents a portion of a document whose content is only indirectly related to the document's main content. Asides are frequently presented as sidebars or call-out boxes.

entries.name: audio
entries.summary: The <audio> HTML element is used to embed sound content in documents. It may contain one or more audio sources, represented using the src attribute or the <source> element: the browser will choose the most suitable one.

entries.name: autocapitalize (attribute)
entries.summary: The autocapitalize global attribute is an enumerated attribute that controls whether inputted text is automatically capitalized and, if so, in what manner. This is relevant to:

entries.name: autocomplete (attribute)
entries.summary: The HTML autocomplete attribute lets web developers specify what if any permission the user agent has to provide automated assistance in filling out form field values, as well as guidance to the browser as to the type o…

entries.name: autocorrect (attribute)
entries.summary: The autocorrect global attribute is an enumerated attribute that controls whether autocorrection of editable text is enabled for spelling and/or punctuation errors.

entries.name: autofocus (attribute)
entries.summary: The autofocus global attribute is a Boolean attribute indicating whether the element should be focused on page load or, if it is nested inside a <dialog> or popover element, when the <dialog> or popover is shown.

entries.name: b
entries.summary: The <b> HTML element is used to draw the reader's attention to the element's contents, which are not otherwise granted special importance.

entries.name: base
entries.summary: The <base> HTML element specifies the base URL to use for all relative URLs in a document. There can be only one <base> element in a document.

entries.name: bdi
entries.summary: The <bdi> HTML element tells the browser's bidirectional algorithm to treat the text it contains in isolation from its surrounding text.

entries.name: bdo
entries.summary: The <bdo> HTML element overrides the current directionality of text, so that the text within is rendered in a different direction.

entries.name: blockquote
entries.summary: The <blockquote> HTML element indicates that the enclosed text is an extended quotation. Usually, this is rendered visually by indentation (see Notes for how to change it).

entries.name: body
entries.summary: The <body> HTML element represents the content of an HTML document. There can be only one <body> element in a document.

entries.name: br
entries.summary:
The
HTML element produces a line break in text (carriage-return). It is useful for writing a poem or an address, where the division of lines is significant.

entries.name: button
entries.summary: The <button> HTML element is an interactive element activated by a user with a mouse, keyboard, finger, voice command, or other assistive technology.

entries.name: canvas
entries.summary: Use the <canvas> with either the canvas scripting API or the WebGL API to draw graphics and animations.

entries.name: caption
entries.summary: The <caption> HTML element specifies the caption (or title) of a table, providing the table an accessible name or accessible description.

entries.name: capture (attribute)
entries.summary: The capture attribute specifies that, optionally, a new file should be captured, and which device should be used to capture that new media of a type defined by the accept attribute.

entries.name: cite
entries.summary: The <cite> HTML element is used to mark up the title of a creative work. The reference may be in an abbreviated form according to context-appropriate conventions related to citation metadata.

entries.name: class (attribute)
entries.summary: The class global attribute is a list of the classes of the element, separated by ASCII whitespace.

entries.name: code
entries.summary: The <code> HTML element displays its contents styled in a fashion intended to indicate that the text is a short fragment of computer code.

entries.name: col
entries.summary: The <col> HTML element defines one or more columns in a column group represented by its parent <colgroup> element. The <col> element is only valid as a child of a <colgroup> element that has no span attribute defined.

entries.name: colgroup
entries.summary: The <colgroup> HTML element defines a group of columns within a table.

entries.name: content (attribute)
entries.summary: The content attribute specifies the value of a metadata name defined by the <meta> name attribute. It takes a string as its value, and the expected syntax varies depending on the name value used.

entries.name: contenteditable (attribute)
entries.summary: The contenteditable global attribute is an enumerated attribute indicating if the element should be editable by the user. If so, the browser modifies its widget to allow editing.

entries.name: crossorigin (attribute)
entries.summary: The crossorigin attribute, valid on the

entries.name: data
entries.summary: The <data> HTML element links a given piece of content with a machine-readable translation. If the content is time- or date-related, the <time> element must be used.

entries.name: data-* (attribute)
entries.summary: The data-* global attributes form a class of attributes called custom data attributes, that allow proprietary information to be exchanged between the HTML and its DOM representation by scripts.

entries.name: datalist
entries.summary: The <datalist> HTML element contains a set of <option> elements that represent the permissible or recommended options available to choose from within other controls.

entries.name: dd
entries.summary: The <dd> HTML element provides the description, definition, or value for the preceding term (<dt>) in a description list (<dl>).

entries.name: del
entries.summary: The <del> HTML element represents a range of text that has been deleted from a document. This can be used when rendering "track changes" or source code diff information, for example.

entries.name: details
entries.summary: The <details> HTML element creates a disclosure widget in which information is visible only when the widget is toggled into an open state. A summary or label must be provided using the <summary> element.

entries.name: dfn
entries.summary: The <dfn> HTML element indicates a term to be defined. The <dfn> element should be used in a complete definition statement, where the full definition of the term can be one of the following:

entries.name: dialog
entries.summary: The <dialog> HTML element represents a modal or non-modal dialog box or other interactive component, such as a dismissible alert, inspector, or subwindow.

entries.name: dir (attribute)
entries.summary: The dir global attribute is an enumerated attribute that indicates the directionality of the element's text.

entries.name: dirname (attribute)
entries.summary: The dirname attribute can be used on the <textarea> element and several <input> types and describes the directionality of the element's text content during form submission.

entries.name: disabled (attribute)
entries.summary: The Boolean disabled attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, focusable, or even submitted with the form. The user can neither edit nor focus on the control, nor its form control descendants.

entries.name: div
entries.summary: The <div> HTML element is the generic container for flow content.

entries.name: dl
entries.summary: The <dl> HTML element represents a description list. The element encloses a list of groups of terms (specified using the <dt> element) and descriptions (provided by <dd> elements).

entries.name: draggable (attribute)
entries.summary: The draggable global attribute is an enumerated attribute that indicates whether the element can be dragged, either with native browser behavior or the HTML Drag and Drop API.

entries.name: dt
entries.summary: The <dt> HTML element specifies a term in a description or definition list, and as such must be used inside a <dl> element.

entries.name: elementtiming (attribute)
entries.summary: The elementtiming attribute is used to indicate that an element is flagged for tracking by PerformanceObserver objects using the "element" type. For more details, see the PerformanceElementTiming interface.

entries.name: em
entries.summary: The <em> HTML element marks text that has stress emphasis. The <em> element can be nested, with each level of nesting indicating a greater degree of emphasis.

entries.name: embed
entries.summary: The <embed> HTML element embeds external content at the specified point in the document. This content is provided by an external application or other source of interactive content such as a browser plug-in.

entries.name: enterkeyhint (attribute)
entries.summary: The enterkeyhint global attribute is an enumerated attribute defining what action label (or icon) to present for the enter key on virtual keyboards.

entries.name: exportparts (attribute)
entries.summary: The exportparts global attribute allows you to select and style elements existing in nested shadow trees, by exporting their part names.

entries.name: fencedframe
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: fetchpriority (attribute)
entries.summary: The fetchpriority attribute allows a developer to signal that fetching a particular image early in the loading process has more or less impact on user experience than a browser can reasonably infer when assigning an int…

entries.name: fieldset
entries.summary: The <fieldset> HTML element is used to group several controls as well as labels (<label>) within a web form.

entries.name: figcaption
entries.summary: The <figcaption> HTML element represents a caption or legend describing the rest of the contents of its parent <figure> element, providing the <figure> an accessible name.

entries.name: figure
entries.summary: The <figure> HTML element represents self-contained content, potentially with an optional caption, which is specified using the <figcaption> element.

entries.name: footer
entries.summary: The <footer> HTML element represents a footer for its nearest ancestor sectioning content or sectioning root element.

entries.name: for (attribute)
entries.summary: The for attribute is an allowed attribute for <label> and <output>. When used on a <label> element it indicates the form element that this label describes.

entries.name: form
entries.summary: The <form> HTML element represents a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information.

entries.name: form (attribute)
entries.summary: The form HTML attribute associates a form-associated element with a <form> element within the same document.

entries.name: geolocation
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: head
entries.summary: The <head> HTML element contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, like its title, scripts, and style sheets. There can be only one <head> element in an HTML document.

entries.name: header
entries.summary: The <header> HTML element represents introductory content, typically a group of introductory or navigational aids. It may contain some heading elements but also a logo, a search form, an author name, and other elements.

entries.name: heading elements
entries.summary: The <h1> to <h6> HTML elements represent six levels of section headings. <h1> is the highest section level and <h6> is the lowest.

entries.name: hgroup
entries.summary:
The
HTML element represents a heading and related content. It groups a single

–

element with one or more

.

entries.name: hidden (attribute)
entries.summary: The hidden global attribute is an enumerated attribute indicating that the browser should not render the contents of the element.

entries.name: hr
entries.summary: The <hr> HTML element represents a thematic break between paragraph-level elements: for example, a change of scene in a story, or a shift of topic within a section.

entries.name: html
entries.summary: The <html> HTML element represents the root (top-level element) of an HTML document, so it is also referred to as the root element. All other elements must be descendants of this element.

entries.name: i
entries.summary: The <i> HTML element represents a range of text that is set off from the normal text for some reason, such as idiomatic text, technical terms, taxonomical designations, among others.

entries.name: id (attribute)
entries.summary: The id global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique within the entire document.

entries.name: iframe
entries.summary: The <iframe> HTML element represents a nested browsing context, embedding another HTML page into the current one.

entries.name: img
entries.summary: The HTML element embeds an image into the document.

entries.name: inert (attribute)
entries.summary: The inert global attribute is a Boolean attribute indicating that the element and all of its flat tree descendants become inert. The inert attribute can be added to sections of content that should not be interactive.

entries.name: input
entries.summary: The <input> HTML element is used to create interactive controls for web-based forms in order to accept data from the user; a wide variety of types of input data and control widgets are available, depending on the device…

entries.name: input type="button"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type button are rendered as push buttons, which can be programmed to control custom functionality anywhere on a webpage as required when assigned an event handler function (typically for the click ev…

entries.name: input type="checkbox"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type checkbox are rendered by default as boxes that are checked (ticked) when activated, like you might see in an official government paper form.

entries.name: input type="color"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type color provide a user interface element that lets a user specify a color, either by using a visual color picker interface or by entering the color into a text field in a CSS color value format.

entries.name: input type="date"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type="date" create input fields that let the user enter a date. The appearance of the date picker input UI varies based on the browser and operating system.

entries.name: input type="datetime-local"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type datetime-local create input controls that let the user easily enter both a date and a time, including the year, month, and day as well as the time in hours and minutes.

entries.name: input type="email"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type email are used to let the user enter and edit an email address, or, if the multiple attribute is specified, a list of email addresses.

entries.name: input type="file"
entries.summary: <input> elements with type="file" let the user choose one or more files from their device storage.

entries.name: input type="hidden"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type hidden let web developers include data that cannot be seen or modified by users when a form is submitted.

entries.name: input type="image"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type image are used to create graphical submit buttons, i.e., submit buttons that take the form of an image rather than text.

entries.name: input type="month"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type month create input fields that let the user enter a month and year allowing a month and year to be easily entered.

entries.name: input type="number"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type number are used to let the user enter a number. They include built-in validation to reject non-numerical entries.

entries.name: input type="password"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type password provide a way for the user to securely enter a password.

entries.name: input type="radio"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type radio are generally used in radio groups—collections of radio buttons describing a set of related options.

entries.name: input type="range"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type range let the user specify a numeric value which must be no less than a given value, and no more than another given value. The precise value, however, is not considered important.

entries.name: input type="reset"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type reset are rendered as buttons, with a default click event handler that resets all inputs in the form to their initial values.

entries.name: input type="search"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type search are text fields designed for the user to enter search queries into. These are functionally identical to text inputs, but may be styled differently by the user agent.

entries.name: input type="submit"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type submit are rendered as buttons. When the click event occurs (typically because the user clicked the button), the user agent attempts to submit the form to the server.

entries.name: input type="tel"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type tel are used to let the user enter and edit a telephone number.

entries.name: input type="text"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type text create basic single-line text fields.

entries.name: input type="time"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type time create input fields designed to let the user easily enter a time (hours and minutes, and optionally seconds).

entries.name: input type="url"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type url are used to let the user enter and edit a URL.

entries.name: input type="week"
entries.summary: <input> elements of type week create input fields allowing easy entry of a year plus the ISO 8601 week number during that year (i.e., week 1 to 52 or 53).

entries.name: inputmode (attribute)
entries.summary: The inputmode global attribute is an enumerated attribute that hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents.

entries.name: ins
entries.summary: The <ins> HTML element represents a range of text that has been added to a document. You can use the <del> element to similarly represent a range of text that has been deleted from the document.

entries.name: integrity (attribute)
entries.summary: The integrity attribute provides a mechanism for a developer to assert that a linked script or stylesheet must have a particular content.

entries.name: is (attribute)
entries.summary: Note: Safari does not plan to support customized built-in elements and browser vendors are exploring alternative solutions to customizing built-ins. Check the browser compatibility section for support information.

entries.name: itemid (attribute)
entries.summary: The itemid global attribute provides microdata in the form of a unique, global identifier of an item.

entries.name: itemprop (attribute)
entries.summary: The itemprop global attribute is used to add properties to an item. Every HTML element can have an itemprop attribute specified, and an itemprop consists of a name-value pair.

entries.name: itemref (attribute)
entries.summary: Properties that are not descendants of an element with the itemscope attribute can be associated with an item using the global attribute itemref.

entries.name: itemscope (attribute)
entries.summary: itemscope is a boolean global attribute that defines the scope of associated metadata.

entries.name: itemtype (attribute)
entries.summary: The global attribute itemtype specifies the URL of the vocabulary that will be used to define itemprop's (item properties) in the data structure.

entries.name: kbd
entries.summary: The <kbd> HTML element represents a span of inline text denoting textual user input from a keyboard, voice input, or any other text entry device.

entries.name: label
entries.summary: The <label> HTML element represents a caption for an item in a user interface.

entries.name: lang (attribute)
entries.summary: The lang global attribute helps define the language of an element: the language that non-editable elements are written in, or the language that the editable elements should be written in by the user.

entries.name: legend
entries.summary: The <legend> HTML element represents a caption for the content of its parent <fieldset>.

entries.name: li
entries.summary: The <li> HTML element is used to represent an item in a list. It must be contained in a parent element: an ordered list (<ol>), an unordered list (<ul>), or a menu (<menu>).

entries.name: link
entries.summary: The <link> HTML element specifies relationships between the current document and an external resource.

entries.name: main
entries.summary: The <main> HTML element represents the dominant content of the <body> of a document.

entries.name: map
entries.summary: The <map> HTML element is used with <area> elements to define an image map (a clickable link area).

entries.name: mark
entries.summary: The <mark> HTML element represents text which is marked or highlighted for reference or notation purposes due to the marked passage's relevance in the enclosing context.

entries.name: max (attribute)
entries.summary: The max attribute defines the maximum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the value of the element is greater than this, the element fails validation.

entries.name: maxlength (attribute)
entries.summary: The maxlength attribute defines the maximum string length that the user can enter into an <input> or <textarea>. The attribute must have an integer value of 0 or higher.

entries.name: menu
entries.summary: The <menu> HTML element is described in the HTML specification as a semantic alternative to <ul>, but treated by browsers (and exposed through the accessibility tree) as no different than <ul>.

entries.name: meta
entries.summary: The <meta> HTML element represents metadata that cannot be represented by other meta-related elements, such as <base>, <link>, <script>, <style>, or <title>.

entries.name: meta.http-equiv
entries.summary: The http-equiv attribute of the <meta> element allows you to provide processing instructions for the browser as if the response that returned the document included certain HTTP headers.

entries.name: meta.name
entries.summary: The name attribute of the <meta> element provides metadata in name-value pairs. When a <meta> element has a name attribute, a content attribute defines the corresponding value.

entries.name: meta.name.color-scheme
entries.summary: The color-scheme value for the name attribute of the <meta> element indicates a suggested color scheme that user agents should use for a page.

entries.name: meta.name.referrer
entries.summary: The referrer value for the name attribute of the <meta> element controls the HTTP Referer header of requests sent from the document.

entries.name: meta.name.robots
entries.summary: The robots value for the name attribute of the <meta> element (often called a "robots tag") defines the crawl and indexing behavior that web crawlers should use with the page.

entries.name: meta.name.text-scale
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: meta.name.theme-color
entries.summary: The theme-color value for the name attribute of the <meta> element indicates a suggested color that user agents should use to customize the display of the page or of the surrounding user interface.

entries.name: meta.name.viewport
entries.summary: The viewport value for the name attribute of a <meta> element gives hints about how the viewport should be sized.

entries.name: meter
entries.summary: The <meter> HTML element represents either a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value.

entries.name: min (attribute)
entries.summary: The min attribute defines the minimum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the value of the element is less than this, the element fails validation.

entries.name: minlength (attribute)
entries.summary: The minlength attribute defines the minimum string length that the user can enter into an <input> or <textarea>. The attribute must have an integer value of 0 or higher.

entries.name: multiple (attribute)
entries.summary: The Boolean multiple attribute, if set, means the form control accepts one or more values. The attribute is valid for the email and file input types and the <select>.

entries.name: nav
entries.summary: The <nav> HTML element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents.

entries.name: nonce (attribute)
entries.summary: The nonce global attribute is a content attribute defining a cryptographic nonce ("number used once") which can be used by Content Security Policy to determine whether or not a given fetch will be allowed to proceed for…

entries.name: noscript
entries.summary: The <noscript> HTML element defines a section of HTML to be inserted if a script type on the page is unsupported or if scripting is currently turned off in the browser.

entries.name: object
entries.summary: The <object> HTML element represents an external resource, which can be treated as an image, a nested browsing context, or a resource to be handled by a plugin.

entries.name: ol
entries.summary: The <ol> HTML element represents an ordered list of items — typically rendered as a numbered list.

entries.name: optgroup
entries.summary: The <optgroup> HTML element creates a grouping of options within a <select> element.

entries.name: option
entries.summary: The <option> HTML element is used to define an item contained in a <select>, an <optgroup>, or a <datalist> element. As such, <option> can represent menu items in popups and other lists of items in an HTML document.

entries.name: output
entries.summary: The <output> HTML element is a container element into which a site or app can inject the results of a calculation or the outcome of a user action.

entries.name: p
entries.summary:
The

HTML element represents a paragraph.

entries.name: part (attribute)
entries.summary: The part global attribute contains a space-separated list of the part names of the element. Part names allows CSS to select and style specific elements in a shadow tree via the ::part pseudo-element.

entries.name: pattern (attribute)
entries.summary: The pattern attribute specifies a regular expression the form control's value should match.

entries.name: picture
entries.summary: The HTML element contains zero or more elements and one element to offer alternative versions of an image for different display/device scenarios.

entries.name: placeholder (attribute)
entries.summary: The placeholder attribute defines the text displayed in a form control when the control has no value.

entries.name: popover (attribute)
entries.summary: The popover global attribute is used to designate an element as a popover element.

entries.name: pre
entries.summary: The <pre> HTML element represents preformatted text which is to be presented exactly as written in the HTML file. The text is typically rendered using a non-proportional, or monospaced font.

entries.name: progress
entries.summary: The <progress> HTML element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.

entries.name: q
entries.summary: The <q> HTML element indicates that the enclosed text is a short inline quotation. Most modern browsers implement this by surrounding the text in quotation marks.

entries.name: readonly (attribute)
entries.summary: The Boolean readonly attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, meaning the user can not edit the control.

entries.name: Reference.Attributes
entries.summary: Elements in HTML have attributes; these are additional values that configure the elements or adjust their behavior in various ways to meet the criteria the users want.

entries.name: Reference.Elements
entries.summary: This page lists all the HTML elements, which are created using tags.

entries.name: Reference.Global attributes
entries.summary: Global attributes are attributes common to all HTML elements; they can be used on all elements, though they may have no effect on some elements.

entries.name: rel (attribute)
entries.summary: The rel attribute defines the relationship between a linked resource and the current document. Valid on <link>, <a>, <area>, and <form>, the supported values depend on the element on which the attribute is found.

entries.name: rel.alternate stylesheet (attribute)
entries.summary: The alternate stylesheet keyword pair, when used as a value for the rel attribute of the <link> element, indicates that the target resource is an alternative style sheet.

entries.name: rel.compression-dictionary (attribute)
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: rel.dns-prefetch (attribute)
entries.summary: The dns-prefetch keyword for the rel attribute of the <link> element is a hint to browsers that the user is likely to need resources from the target resource's origin, and therefore the browser can likely improve the us…

entries.name: rel.manifest (attribute)
entries.summary: The manifest keyword for the rel attribute of the <link> element indicates that the target resource is a Web app manifest.

entries.name: rel.me (attribute)
entries.summary: The me keyword for the rel attribute of the <link> and <a> elements indicates that the current resource is represented by the linked party. The me value was introduced in the XHTML Friends Network (XFN) specification.

entries.name: rel.modulepreload (attribute)
entries.summary: The modulepreload keyword, for the rel attribute of the <link> element, provides a declarative way to preemptively fetch a module script, parse and compile it, and store it in the document's module map for later executi…

entries.name: rel.noopener (attribute)
entries.summary: The noopener keyword for the rel attribute of the <a>, <area>, and <form> elements instructs the browser to navigate to the target resource without granting the new browsing context access to the document that opened it…

entries.name: rel.noreferrer (attribute)
entries.summary: The noreferrer keyword for the rel attribute of the <a>, <area>, and <form> elements instructs the browser, when navigating to the target resource, to omit the Referer header and otherwise leak no referrer information —…

entries.name: rel.preconnect (attribute)
entries.summary: The preconnect keyword for the rel attribute of the <link> element is a hint to browsers that the user is likely to need resources from the target resource's origin, and therefore the browser can likely improve the user…

entries.name: rel.prefetch (attribute)
entries.summary: The prefetch keyword for the rel attribute of the <link> element provides a hint to browsers that the user is likely to need the target resource for future navigations, and therefore the browser can likely improve the u…

entries.name: rel.preload (attribute)
entries.summary: The preload value of the <link> element's rel attribute lets you declare fetch requests in the HTML's <head>, specifying resources that your page will need very soon, which you want to start loading early in the page li…

entries.name: required (attribute)
entries.summary: The Boolean required attribute, if present, indicates that the user must specify a value for the input before the owning form can be submitted.

entries.name: rp
entries.summary: The <rp> HTML element is used to provide fall-back parentheses for browsers that do not support display of ruby annotations using the <ruby> element.

entries.name: rt
entries.summary: The <rt> HTML element specifies the ruby text component of a ruby annotation, which is used to provide pronunciation, translation, or transliteration information for East Asian typography.

entries.name: ruby
entries.summary: The <ruby> HTML element represents small annotations that are rendered above, below, or next to base text, usually used for showing the pronunciation of East Asian characters.

entries.name: s
entries.summary: The <s> HTML element renders text with a strikethrough, or a line through it. Use the <s> element to represent things that are no longer relevant or no longer accurate.

entries.name: samp
entries.summary: The <samp> HTML element is used to enclose inline text which represents sample (or quoted) output from a computer program.

entries.name: script
entries.summary: The <script> HTML element is used to embed executable code or data; this is typically used to embed or refer to JavaScript code.

entries.name: script.type
entries.summary: The type attribute of the <script> element indicates the type of script represented by the element: a classic script, an import map, a JavaScript module, speculation rules, or a data block.

entries.name: script.type.importmap
entries.summary: The importmap value of the type attribute of the <script> element indicates that the body of the element contains an import map.

entries.name: script.type.speculationrules
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: search
entries.summary: The <search> HTML element is a container representing the parts of the document or application with form controls or other content related to performing a search or filtering operation.

entries.name: section
entries.summary: The <section> HTML element represents a generic standalone section of a document, which doesn't have a more specific semantic element to represent it. Sections should always have a heading, with very few exceptions.

entries.name: select
entries.summary: The <select> HTML element represents a control that provides a menu of options.

entries.name: selectedcontent
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: size (attribute)
entries.summary: The size attribute defines the width of the <input> and the height of the <select> element. For an input element, it defines the number of characters that the user agent allows the user to see when editing the value.

entries.name: slot
entries.summary: The <slot> HTML element is a placeholder inside a Web Component that you can fill with your own markup when the component is used. This lets you create separate DOM trees and present them together.

entries.name: slot (attribute)
entries.summary: The slot global attribute assigns a slot in a shadow DOM shadow tree to an element: An element with a slot attribute is assigned to the slot created by the <slot> element whose name attribute's value matches that slot a…

entries.name: small
entries.summary: The <small> HTML element represents side-comments and small print, like copyright and legal text, independent of its styled presentation.

entries.name: source
entries.summary: The <source> HTML element specifies one or more media resources for the <picture>, <audio>, and <video> elements. It is a void element, which means that it has no content and does not require a closing tag.

entries.name: span
entries.summary: The <span> HTML element is a generic inline container for phrasing content, which does not inherently represent anything.

entries.name: spellcheck (attribute)
entries.summary: The spellcheck global attribute is an enumerated attribute that defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors.

entries.name: step (attribute)
entries.summary: The step attribute is a number that specifies the granularity that the value must adhere to or the keyword any.

entries.name: strong
entries.summary: The <strong> HTML element indicates that its contents have strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Browsers typically render the contents in bold type.

entries.name: style
entries.summary: The <style> HTML element contains style information for a document, or part of a document. It contains CSS, which is applied to the contents of the document containing the <style> element.

entries.name: style (attribute)
entries.summary: The style global attribute contains CSS styling declarations to be applied to the element. Note that it is recommended for styles to be defined in a separate file or files.

entries.name: sub
entries.summary: The <sub> HTML element specifies inline text which should be displayed as subscript for solely typographical reasons. Subscripts are typically rendered with a lowered baseline using smaller text.

entries.name: summary
entries.summary: The <summary> HTML element specifies a summary, caption, or legend for a <details> element's disclosure box. Clicking the <summary> element toggles the state of the parent <details> element open and closed.

entries.name: sup
entries.summary: The <sup> HTML element specifies inline text which is to be displayed as superscript for solely typographical reasons. Superscripts are usually rendered with a raised baseline using smaller text.

entries.name: tabindex (attribute)
entries.summary: The tabindex global attribute allows developers to make HTML elements focusable, allow or prevent them from being sequentially focusable (usually with the Tab key, hence the name) and determine their relative ordering f…

entries.name: table
entries.summary: The <table> HTML element represents tabular data—that is, information presented in a two-dimensional table comprised of rows and columns of cells containing data.

entries.name: tbody
entries.summary: The <tbody> HTML element encapsulates a set of table rows (<tr> elements), indicating that they comprise the body of a table's (main) data.

entries.name: td
entries.summary: The <td> HTML element defines a cell of a table that contains data and may be used as a child of the <tr> element.

entries.name: template
entries.summary: The <template> HTML element serves as a mechanism for holding HTML fragments, which can either be used later via JavaScript or generated immediately into shadow DOM.

entries.name: textarea
entries.summary: The <textarea> HTML element represents a multi-line plain-text editing control, useful when you want to allow users to enter a sizeable amount of free-form text, for example a comment on a review or feedback form.

entries.name: tfoot
entries.summary: The <tfoot> HTML element encapsulates a set of table rows (<tr> elements), indicating that they comprise the foot of a table with information about the table's columns.

entries.name: th
entries.summary: The <th> HTML element defines a cell as the header of a group of table cells and may be used as a child of the <tr> element. The exact nature of this group is defined by the scope and headers attributes.

entries.name: thead
entries.summary: The <thead> HTML element encapsulates a set of table rows (<tr> elements), indicating that they comprise the head of a table with information about the table's columns.

entries.name: time
entries.summary: The <time> HTML element represents a specific period in time.

entries.name: title
entries.summary: The <title> HTML element defines the document's title that is shown in a browser's title bar or a page's tab. It only contains text; HTML tags within the element, if any, are also treated as plain text.

entries.name: title (attribute)
entries.summary: The title global attribute contains text representing advisory information related to the element it belongs to.

entries.name: tr
entries.summary: The <tr> HTML element defines a row of cells in a table. The row's cells can then be established using a mix of <td> (data cell) and <th> (header cell) elements.

entries.name: track
entries.summary: The <track> HTML element is used as a child of the media elements, <audio> and <video>.

entries.name: translate (attribute)
entries.summary: The translate global attribute is an enumerated attribute that is used to specify whether an element's translatable attribute values and its Text node children should be translated when the page is localized, or whether…

entries.name: u
entries.summary: The <u> HTML element represents a span of inline text which should be rendered in a way that indicates that it has a non-textual annotation.

entries.name: ul
entries.summary: The <ul> HTML element represents an unordered list of items, typically rendered as a bulleted list.

entries.name: var
entries.summary: The <var> HTML element represents the name of a variable in a mathematical expression or a programming context.

entries.name: video
entries.summary: The <video> HTML element embeds a media player which supports video playback into the document. You can use <video> for audio content as well, but the <audio> element may provide a more appropriate user experience.

entries.name: virtualkeyboardpolicy (attribute)
entries.summary: Experimental: This is an experimental technologyCheck the Browser compatibility table carefully before using this in production.

entries.name: wbr
entries.summary: The <wbr> HTML element represents a word break opportunity—a position within text where the browser may optionally break a line, though its line-breaking rules would not otherwise create a break at that location.

entries.name: writingsuggestions (attribute)
entries.summary: The writingsuggestions global attribute is an enumerated attribute indicating if browser-provided writing suggestions should be enabled under the scope of the element or not.
